text: A company replaces a $400,000 datacenter purchase with a monthly AWS bill. Which financial benefit of the cloud does this illustrate?

options.A: Trading capital expense for variable expense
options.B: Increasing the depreciation schedule of owned hardware

explanation_en: Moving from an up-front hardware purchase (CapEx) to pay-as-you-go usage (OpEx / variable expense) is one of the six advantages of cloud computing. AWS never eliminates all cost, and pay-as-you-go is by definition not a fixed monthly amount.
tip: CapEx = you buy the box up front. OpEx = you pay for what you use. Any option promising ZERO cost or a GUARANTEED FIXED bill is wrong - pay-as-you-go is variable by definition.

text: Which statement best distinguishes elasticity from scalability?

options.A: Elasticity only adds capacity; scalability adds and removes it
options.B: Elasticity adds and removes capacity to match demand; scalability is the ability to increase capacity
options.C: They are two names for the same behavior
options.D: Elasticity applies only to storage and scalability only to compute

explanation_en: Scalability is about being able to INCREASE capacity. Elasticity is about CHANGING capacity in both directions automatically as demand rises and falls.
tip: Read the verbs. SCALABILITY = add / increase (one direction). ELASTICITY = increase OR decrease / change (both directions, automatic). The exam separates them on that single word.

text: Which of the following are benefits AWS claims for cloud computing? (Choose two.)

options.B: Greater application security than any on-premises design
options.C: Benefit from massive economies of scale
options.D: Elimination of the need for any security configuration

explanation_en: 'Go global in minutes' and 'benefit from massive economies of scale' are two of the six advantages of cloud computing. AWS never claims that moving to the cloud automatically makes an application more secure or removes your security responsibilities.
tip: 'GREATER APPLICATION SECURITY' is the universal distractor in this book - AWS never promises it. The real six: trade CapEx for OpEx, economies of scale, stop guessing capacity, increase speed and agility, stop running datacenters, go global in minutes.

text: A workload runs partly in a company datacenter and partly on AWS, connected over Direct Connect. Which deployment model is this?
explanation_en: A hybrid deployment mixes cloud resources with existing on-premises infrastructure. Multi-cloud would mean two or more cloud providers, not cloud plus on-premises.
tip: Three models: CLOUD (all in), ON-PREMISES/private (all in your building), HYBRID (both, connected). If the stem mentions a datacenter AND AWS together, it is hybrid. Two cloud VENDORS would be multi-cloud - different question.

text: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the customer?
explanation_en: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, facilities, media disposal). The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud, which includes security groups, IAM, guest OS patching, and data encryption choices.
tip: One line settles every shared-responsibility question: AWS secures the CLOUD, you secure what you put IN it. If you can click it, configure it, or edit it, you own it.

text: What is a hypervisor responsible for?

options.A: Routing network traffic between availability zones
options.B: Partitioning physical hardware into multiple virtual machines
options.C: Encrypting data stored on EBS volumes
options.D: Distributing incoming requests across EC2 instances

explanation_en: A hypervisor is software that virtualizes a physical server, allowing several isolated virtual machines to run on it. It does not route, encrypt, or balance load.
tip: Hypervisor = SOFTWARE that partitions one physical machine into many virtual ones. It is not hardware, not a network device, and AWS - not you - manages it.

text: How does AWS achieve the scale required to serve millions of customers? (Choose two.)

options.A: By running an enormous number of servers
options.B: By limiting each account to a single region
options.C: Through heavy automation of provisioning and management
options.D: By requiring customers to purchase reserved capacity

explanation_en: AWS scale comes from the sheer number of servers it operates combined with automation that provisions and manages them without human intervention. Accounts are not limited to one region, and reservations are optional.
tip: AWS scales with QUANTITY OF SERVERS plus AUTOMATION. Any option that restricts the customer (one region, mandatory reservations) is describing a limitation, not a scaling mechanism.

text: Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework focuses on running and monitoring systems and continually improving processes?
explanation_en: Operational excellence covers running, monitoring, and improving operational procedures, with automation as a core practice.
tip: Pillar keywords: OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE = automate and improve processes. RELIABILITY = recover from failure. PERFORMANCE EFFICIENCY = use resources efficiently as demand changes. COST OPTIMIZATION = avoid unneeded spend. SECURITY = protect data and identity. SUSTAINABILITY = reduce environmental impact.

text: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
explanation_en: The six pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. Scalability is a property of a system, not a pillar.
tip: Memorize the six and reject everything else. The recurring fakes are SCALABILITY, RESILIENCY, AVAILABILITY, ELASTICITY and AGILITY - all real concepts, none of them pillars.

text: An architect designs a system that automatically replaces failed instances and recovers from an availability zone outage. Which pillar is being applied?
explanation_en: Reliability is about a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, including automatic recovery from failure.
tip: RELIABILITY always means REPLACE or RECOVER the failed resource. If the sentence describes automatic recovery, redundancy across AZs, or replacing a broken instance, it is reliability.

text: Which cloud service model gives the customer the most control over the underlying operating system?
explanation_en: IaaS (for example EC2) hands you the virtual machine, so you manage the operating system. PaaS abstracts the OS away, and SaaS abstracts the whole application.
tip: Order of control, most to least: IaaS (EC2 - you own the OS) > PaaS (Elastic Beanstalk - you own the code) > SaaS (you just log in). More control also means more responsibility.

text: Which AWS offering is the clearest example of Software as a Service?
explanation_en: WorkMail is a finished application you simply consume - the definition of SaaS. EC2 and EBS are IaaS, and Elastic Beanstalk is PaaS.
tip: SaaS = a finished product you just use (WorkMail, WorkDocs, Chime, QuickSight). PaaS = you supply code (Beanstalk, Lambda). IaaS = you supply the OS (EC2, EBS, VPC).

text: What is the relationship between a region and an availability zone?

options.A: A region is a single datacenter inside an availability zone
options.B: An availability zone contains one or more isolated datacenters inside a region
options.C: An availability zone spans multiple regions for redundancy
options.D: They are two names for the same physical location

explanation_en: A region is a geographic area containing multiple availability zones, and each availability zone is one or more discrete datacenters with independent power and networking.
tip: Nesting order, biggest to smallest: REGION > AVAILABILITY ZONE > datacenter. An AZ never spans regions. AZ letters are randomized per account, so your us-east-1a is not my us-east-1a.

text: A company must keep an application's data physically inside a specific country to satisfy a data-residency law. Which AWS concept lets them do this?
explanation_en: Regions are geographic locations, and data placed in a region stays in that region unless you move it. Selecting a region in the required country satisfies data-residency requirements.
tip: Any question about LAWS, DATA RESIDENCY, SOVEREIGNTY or LATENCY TO USERS is answered by REGION SELECTION. AZs answer availability, edge locations answer content delivery speed.

text: Which AWS service extends AWS infrastructure into a customer's own datacenter?
explanation_en: Outposts places physical AWS-managed racks in the customer's own facility. Local Zones and Wavelength are AWS-operated locations closer to users, not on the customer's premises.
tip: OUTPOSTS = AWS hardware in YOUR building. LOCAL ZONES = AWS metro locations near big cities. WAVELENGTH = inside 5G carrier networks for mobile/AR/VR. Match the word 'on-premises' to Outposts only.

text: Which benefit describes the ability to launch a test environment in minutes instead of waiting weeks for hardware?
explanation_en: Agility is the ability to experiment and deploy quickly because resources are available on demand.
tip: AGILITY = speed of experimentation ('in minutes', 'try an idea', 'fail fast'). Do not confuse it with elasticity (capacity changing with demand) or durability (data not being lost).

text: Which two statements about the AWS shared responsibility model are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: AWS is responsible for the security of the physical infrastructure
options.B: AWS is responsible for the customer's IAM permission design
options.C: The customer is responsible for encrypting their own data
options.D: The customer is responsible for maintaining the hypervisor

explanation_en: AWS secures the underlying infrastructure including hardware, facilities, and the hypervisor. Customers are responsible for their data, including how it is encrypted, and for their identity and access configuration.
tip: Customer side always includes: DATA, IAM, guest OS, network/firewall configuration, encryption choices. AWS side always includes: hardware, facilities, hypervisor, managed-service software, media disposal.

text: Which activity is the clearest example of the cost optimization pillar?

options.B: Enabling MFA on the root user

explanation_en: Cost optimization is about avoiding unnecessary spend, and right-sizing eliminates capacity you are paying for but not using. The other options map to security, reliability, and performance efficiency.
tip: Cost optimization = STOP PAYING FOR WHAT YOU DO NOT USE (right-sizing, deleting idle resources, using Spot/Reserved). It is never about reducing spend to zero, and it is never about adding redundancy.

text: Which of the following AWS services are global rather than regional? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: IAM, Route 53, CloudFront, and Organizations are global services. EC2, RDS, EBS, and Lambda are regional.
tip: Global list to memorize: IAM, Route 53, CloudFront, Organizations, WAF (for CloudFront), and S3 as a service (though buckets live in a region). Everything with an instance or a volume is regional.

text: An organization no longer wants to forecast server needs 18 months in advance. Which cloud advantage addresses this directly?
explanation_en: 'Stop guessing capacity' is the advantage that removes the need to forecast demand, because you scale up or down on demand.
tip: Match the phrasing literally. FORECASTING or GUESSING demand = 'stop guessing capacity'. STAFF and FACILITIES = 'stop running datacenters'. INTERNATIONAL USERS = 'go global in minutes'.

text: Which characteristic makes a website 'static' rather than 'dynamic'?

options.A: It is hosted on more than one server
options.B: Its files are served exactly as stored, with no server-side processing
options.D: It is fronted by a content delivery network

explanation_en: A static site serves stored files unchanged. As soon as a database query or server-side code generates the page, the site is dynamic.
tip: The moment a DATABASE or server-side code is involved, it is DYNAMIC. HTTPS, CDNs and multiple servers say nothing about static versus dynamic.

text: Which two statements correctly describe an AWS edge location? (Choose two.)

options.A: It caches content close to end users
options.B: It is used by Amazon CloudFront
options.C: It hosts EC2 instances for general workloads
options.D: It replaces the need for a region

explanation_en: Edge locations cache CloudFront content near users and also serve Route 53 and Global Accelerator. They do not host general compute workloads and do not replace regions.
tip: Edge locations CACHE, they do not COMPUTE. There are more than 150 of them across 6 continents, plus 13 regional edge caches. If an option puts an EC2 instance in an edge location, it is wrong.

text: Which statement about high availability is correct?

options.A: It guarantees that data is never lost
options.B: It means the system remains operational with minimal manual intervention when a component fails
options.C: It requires the workload to run in more than one region
options.D: It is the same as durability

explanation_en: High availability means the system keeps serving requests when something fails, generally through automatic redundancy and failover. Durability is a separate property about not losing data.
tip: High-availability answers always describe something AUTOMATIC. Also keep DURABILITY (data survives) separate from AVAILABILITY (service responds) - the exam loves swapping them.

text: A team wants to reduce the carbon footprint of its workloads. Which Well-Architected pillar covers this?
explanation_en: Sustainability, the sixth pillar, addresses minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads.
tip: Sustainability is the newest pillar and the one candidates forget exists. Any mention of ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT, CARBON or ENERGY EFFICIENCY points to it.

text: Which two are true about the AWS global infrastructure? (Choose two.)

options.A: Each region contains multiple availability zones
options.B: Availability zones within a region are connected by low-latency links
options.C: All regions are enabled by default in every account
options.D: Availability zones are always in the same building

explanation_en: Regions contain multiple isolated availability zones connected by high-bandwidth, low-latency private networking. Some regions must be explicitly opted into, and AZs are physically separated facilities.
tip: AZs are physically SEPARATE (different power, cooling, flood plain) but NETWORKED with low latency - that is why synchronous Multi-AZ replication works. 'Same building' is always wrong.

text: A startup cannot predict whether it will have 100 or 100,000 users next month. Which two cloud characteristics address this uncertainty? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: Elasticity lets capacity grow and shrink with actual demand, and pay-as-you-go means the bill follows that capacity instead of a fixed purchase.
tip: Unpredictable demand is always answered by ELASTICITY plus PAY-AS-YOU-GO. Durability and physical security are real benefits but answer different questions.

text: Which AWS service uses natural language processing to determine the sentiment of customer reviews?
explanation_en: Comprehend is the natural language processing service that extracts sentiment, entities, and key phrases from text.
tip: AI service map: COMPREHEND = text meaning/sentiment. REKOGNITION = images and video. TEXTRACT = scanned documents and forms. TRANSCRIBE = speech to text. POLLY = text to speech. TRANSLATE = languages. LEX = chatbots. KENDRA = enterprise search. SAGEMAKER = build your own model.

text: A company needs to build a customer-service chatbot with voice and text. Which two services would it combine? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: Lex provides the conversational interface and Polly converts the response text into lifelike speech. Redshift and Glue are analytics and ETL services.
tip: LEX + POLLY is the classic chatbot pair: Lex understands, Polly speaks. If the stem adds 'transcribe what the caller said', add Transcribe.

text: What does 'virtualization' allow a cloud provider to do?

options.A: Run one operating system across many physical servers
options.B: Divide one physical server into multiple isolated virtual servers
options.C: Eliminate the need for physical hardware entirely
options.D: Guarantee that no two customers share a datacenter

explanation_en: Virtualization partitions physical hardware so multiple isolated virtual machines can share it efficiently. Physical hardware still exists, and multi-tenancy is normal.
tip: Virtualization = PARTITION one machine into many. Any option claiming the cloud has no physical hardware, or that you never share a datacenter, is wrong (dedicated hosts are the paid exception).

text: Which two actions genuinely reduce an AWS bill? (Choose two.)

options.B: Releasing an unattached Elastic IP address

explanation_en: Unattached Elastic IP addresses and unattached EBS volumes both incur charges. Empty S3 buckets and VPCs are free, so deleting them saves nothing.
tip: You only save by deleting things that COST money. Free by themselves: VPCs, empty buckets, security groups, IAM users, route tables. Charged even when idle: unattached EBS volumes, unassociated Elastic IPs, load balancers, NAT gateways, snapshots.

text: To improve the AVAILABILITY of a web application, which approach should be used?

options.A: Load balancing across multiple availability zones
options.B: Auto Scaling based on CPU utilization

explanation_en: Availability is achieved by distributing traffic across redundant resources in multiple availability zones so a single failure does not take the application down.
tip: Read the goal word carefully. AVAILABILITY = load balancing across AZs. CAPACITY / demand = auto scaling. PERFORMANCE for distant users = CloudFront. Bigger instance = vertical scaling, rarely the exam answer.

text: What is the maximum execution time of an AWS Lambda function?
explanation_en: A Lambda function times out after 15 minutes. Longer-running work belongs on EC2, Fargate, or AWS Batch.
tip: 15 MINUTES is a hard number the exam asks directly. If a scenario needs longer processing, the correct service changes to EC2, Fargate or Batch.

text: An application must extract text and field values from scanned invoices. Which service fits best?
explanation_en: Textract reads scanned documents and can associate a form field with its value, which plain OCR and image recognition do not do.
tip: SCANNED DOCUMENTS or FORMS = Textract (it links a field to its value). Photos and video = Rekognition. Meaning of free text = Comprehend. The word 'scan' or 'invoice' is the trigger.

text: Which statement about the AWS Acceptable Use Policy is correct?

options.A: It defines what customers may and may not do with AWS services
options.B: It guarantees a service uptime percentage
options.C: It lists the compliance certifications AWS holds
options.D: It describes the pricing of each service

explanation_en: The Acceptable Use Policy sets out prohibited uses of AWS services. Uptime commitments come from service level agreements and compliance evidence comes from AWS Artifact.
tip: Match the document to its job: AUP = what you may not do. SLA = uptime commitment and credits. ARTIFACT = compliance reports. Well-Architected = design guidance.

text: Which two are true about an application load balancer's role in a highly available design? (Choose two.)

options.A: It routes traffic away from unhealthy targets
options.C: It can distribute traffic across multiple availability zones
options.D: It caches responses to reduce backend load

explanation_en: The load balancer detects unhealthy targets and stops sending them traffic, and it can spread requests across AZs. Replacing instances is the job of Auto Scaling, and caching is the job of CloudFront.
tip: Three separate jobs the exam blends: ALB routes AWAY from failures. AUTO SCALING REPLACES them. CLOUDFRONT CACHES. Pick the verb in the stem.

text: Which two workloads are the best candidates for a serverless architecture? (Choose two.)

options.B: A legacy application requiring a specific kernel module
options.C: An API backend with unpredictable, spiky traffic
options.D: A batch job that runs continuously for four hours

explanation_en: Serverless suits short, event-driven, bursty workloads. Legacy applications needing OS-level control and jobs longer than the Lambda timeout do not fit.
tip: Serverless fits SHORT, EVENT-DRIVEN, SPIKY work. It does not fit anything needing OS control or running past 15 minutes - those two disqualifiers appear in almost every serverless question.

text: What is the correct format of an AWS service endpoint?
explanation_en: Endpoints follow the pattern service.region.amazonaws.com, for example ec2.us-east-1.amazonaws.com.
tip: Service first, region second: ec2.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. Reversing the two is the standard distractor. Global services such as IAM have no region in the endpoint.

text: A company migrates an application to AWS without changing its architecture. What is this migration strategy called?
explanation_en: Rehosting, often called lift and shift, moves an application as-is. Refactoring rewrites it for cloud-native services, repurchasing swaps it for a SaaS product, and retiring decommissions it.
tip: The 7 Rs: REHOST (lift and shift, no change), REPLATFORM (small optimizations), REFACTOR (rewrite cloud-native), REPURCHASE (buy SaaS instead), RETIRE (turn it off), RETAIN (leave it), RELOCATE (move VMware). 'Without changing' always means rehost.

text: Which two statements about AWS managed services are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: AWS handles patching and maintenance of the underlying software
options.B: The customer gains SSH access to the underlying host
options.C: They typically reduce the customer's operational burden
options.D: They remove the customer's responsibility for their own data

explanation_en: Managed services shift patching and maintenance to AWS, reducing operational work. You do not get host access, and responsibility for your own data always remains with you.
tip: The more managed the service, the less you operate - but YOUR DATA IS ALWAYS YOURS. Any option saying AWS becomes responsible for your data is wrong in every domain of this exam.

text: Which service would you use to build, train, and deploy your own custom machine learning model?
explanation_en: SageMaker is the platform for building, training, and deploying custom models. The other services provide pretrained capabilities you consume through an API.
tip: If the stem says YOUR OWN MODEL, TRAIN, or CUSTOM, the answer is SageMaker. Every other AI service is pretrained and consumed through an API call.
